title: Control plane: add region-aware effective routing config snapshot endpoint
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Adds an internal-only API to retrieve effective routing policy snapshots (region-aware, time-bounded) for use by incident bot config-diff collector and change-correlation tooling.
body: ## Context / motivation This PR adds a region-aware config snapshot service + endpoint to retrieve the *effective* routing policy bundle for a given service at a specific point in time. This is a dependency for the incident bot config diff collector (ENG-2843), which needs a reliable source of truth for: (a) what routing/policy config was live at t-30m and (b) what is live now, per region, without scraping configs from multiple stores. We discussed event-sourced snapshots vs on-demand computation; this PR implements the on-demand endpoint with bounded compute + caching, and leaves room to back it with persisted snapshots later. ## What this changes - Adds `config-snapshot` module under control plane that can compute and return the effective routing policy bundle for a `(service, region, at_time)` tuple. - Exposes internal HTTP endpoint: `GET /internal/v1/config-snapshots/effective` with required query params: `service`, `region`, optional `at` (RFC3339). If `at` is omitted, uses current time (server-side). - Adds an internal gRPC client used by Console backend and incident-bot to avoid duplicating auth headers and retry policy. - Implements caching and request coalescing to keep this safe during incidents (many responders / bot retries): 30s TTL by default, singleflight per key, and hard upper bound on compute time. - Adds RBAC + audit logging for access to effective routing policy (service-account only; no end-user tokens). - Normalizes response into a stable schema version so diff tooling can avoid noise from ordering / formatting. ## Endpoint semantics - "Effective" = final routing decision inputs after resolving: base policy bundle + per-region overrides + feature flags + rollout state (canary weights) at the requested time. - Region-aware: region is mandatory; server validates against known regions and uses region-specific override layers. - Time-bounded: if an exact historical value is not available (e.g., flag store retention), server returns the nearest prior value within a bounded lookback window and sets a warning header. Current behavior: allow lookback up to 2h for flags; routing bundles use revision history (git-backed) and can go further. ## Example response (redacted) ```json { "schema_version": "config_snapshot.v1", "service": "gateway", "region": "us-east-1", "requested_at": "2025-02-23T00:18:05Z", "effective_at": "2025-02-23T00:18:00Z", "snapshot_id": "csnap_01JMN9H0Z6B6Y9KQH9RZJ2YF8F", "source_revisions": "policy_rev=7f2c9d1 flags_rev=1708408998 rollout_rev=9b11a80", "bundle_sha256": "1e6c2f...", "redaction": "applied:allowlist_v3", "bundle": {"...": "(see note below)"} } ``` NOTE: In actual responses, `bundle` is included as JSON. In the PR description we’re not pasting real keys; see `docs/config_snapshot_schema.md` for the full schema + field-level allowlist. ## Redaction / safety - This endpoint is **internal** and gated by service-to-service auth; it is still treated as potentially sensitive (e.g., routing destinations, internal hostnames). - Added allowlisted keys by default (same list we expect the incident-bot config diff collector to post in Slack). Non-allowlisted keys are returned as `"<redacted>"` with a per-field audit entry. - Added `X-Redwood-ConfigSnapshot-Redaction-Policy: allowlist_v3` header for downstream tooling to assert what policy was used when generating diffs. ## Performance / reliability considerations - Hard timeout at 800ms for snapshot compute; if exceeded, returns `503` with `retry_after_ms` and a stable error code. - Cache TTL 30s (configurable). Singleflight prevents stampede when multiple incidents are declared simultaneously across regions. - Metrics: `config_snapshot_requests_total`, `config_snapshot_latency_ms`, `config_snapshot_cache_hit_ratio`, `config_snapshot_redactions_total`, `config_snapshot_errors_total` (tagged by error_code, region, service). Cardinality guardrails: service is normalized to a small known set; rejects arbitrary service names. ## Files / areas changed (high level) - `controlplane/configsnapshot/service.go`: snapshot computation pipeline and singleflight cache. - `controlplane/configsnapshot/http_handlers.go`: `/internal/v1/config-snapshots/effective` endpoint. - `controlplane/configsnapshot/redaction/allowlist_v3.yaml`: allowlist policy + test fixtures. - `api/openapi/internal_config_snapshot.yaml`: internal OpenAPI spec + generated client updates. - `rbac/policies/service_accounts.yaml`: allow `incident-bot` and `console-backend` to call endpoint. - `audit/audit_log_rules.yaml`: adds `config_snapshot.read` event type. - `tests/configsnapshot/*`: unit tests (normalization, region overrides, lookback, redaction). ## Commits - controlplane/configsnapshot: add effective snapshot compute pipeline - configsnapshot: add HTTP endpoint + OpenAPI - rbac/audit: gate endpoint & add audit logging - tests: fixtures for multi-region overrides + redaction - metrics: add dashboard panels for snapshot health ## Testing - Unit tests added for: region override resolution, consistent ordering/normalization, redaction allowlist behavior, and lookback behavior when flag history is missing. - Integration test (lightweight) in control plane CI spins a local flag store + policy bundle and validates response schema. ## Rollout plan - Merge behind `controlplane.config_snapshot_endpoint_enabled` (default off in production). - Enable in staging for incident-bot service account first. - SRE to run a small game-day scenario with `at=now` and `at=t-30m` in multiple regions. - If stable for 72h, enable in prod for incident-bot only; Console backend enablement to follow. ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Persisted snapshots to remove dependency on flag store lookback for historical diffs. - Add optional `include_debug=true` gated to restricted channels (returning additional non-postable fields for deep dives). - Wire into incident-bot config diff collector (separate PR in incident-bot repo). --- ## Review conversation (highlights) **Priya Natarajan:** Can we clarify “effective” vs “configured”? Specifically: does this include rollout weights resolved to concrete target sets for the region at time T? If so, we should name it explicitly to avoid confusion downstream. **Ethan Park (author):** Good call. Updated docs and handler comments to define “effective” as post-resolution across policy + flags + rollout state, and added `source_revisions` so diff tooling can explain *why* it changed. Also added `effective_at` separate from `requested_at` when we have to snap to prior history. **Mina Haddad:** Request: stable ordering is key for diff readability. Are we normalizing maps/arrays deterministically? **Ethan Park:** Yes—added `normalizeBundle()` that sorts map keys and applies a canonical ordering to `routes[]` (by `route_id`). Added unit tests that assert stable JSON output for the same inputs across runs. **Marcus Lin:** Redaction policy: even though internal, returning full bundle JSON could include customer-specific routing destinations in some edge cases. We should default to allowlist and require explicit elevated mode for full payload, plus audit log on every call. **Ethan Park:** Agreed. Changed default response to allowlist_v3 and redacts everything else. Added audit event `config_snapshot.read` with `service`, `region`, caller SA, redaction policy, and number of redacted fields. Removed a previously proposed `mode=full` query param from this PR; we can revisit with restricted-mode gating if needed. **Jacob Stein:** For incident bot, we’ll want `t-30m` comparisons. How does lookback behave if the flag store doesn’t have exact history? We should return a clear signal so the bot can say “approximate” rather than claiming exact diffs. **Ethan Park:** Implemented bounded lookback (2h) and added `effective_at` + `X-Redwood-ConfigSnapshot-Warning` header when the snapshot is approximate. Also added explicit error `HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE` when we cannot satisfy within bounds. **Jada Williams:** Please ensure RBAC is service-account only and the endpoint is not reachable from customer VPCs. Also, we should document which SAs are allowed. **Ethan Park:** Done. Endpoint is under `/internal/` and gated in the API gateway to internal mTLS + SA auth. RBAC policy updated; added `docs/internal_endpoints.md` section listing allowed SAs. ## CI status - build-controlplane: PASS - unit-tests: PASS (reran once after fixing flaky time-based assertion in lookback test) - lint/go: PASS - openapi-check: PASS - security-sast: PASS ## Merge Squash merged into `main`.
